title: Ancient Trees in Germany: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Germany protects single trees the way other countries protect buildings, sometimes for bizarre and gnarled growth. 26 cities mapped, 154 trees.
intro: Germany protects individual trees the way other countries protect buildings. A Naturdenkmal is a legal designation attached to one named object, and the reason for it gets written down: Munich's 2021 ordinance protects a lime by the Badenburger See for bizarrer und knorriger Wuchs, bizarre and gnarled growth, and an ash on Leinthalerstrasse for an extremely wide spreading crown, with no age, no measurement and nothing else on file. Nuremberg fits six separately protected trees onto 1.7 hectares of one small park that used to be a quarantine station. Berlin supplies the age: Dicke Marie, in the Tegel Forest, had probably been growing for a long time before the city got its first written mention in 1237. Bamberg supplies the opposite case, four trees with no age recorded for any of them, a pattern that repeats in Stuttgart, Freiburg and Heidelberg, whose registers name and protect a tree without ever measuring it. 26 cities and 154 trees are mapped so far, and the paperwork here is usually better than the dating.
